land.text: 'the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram in central Java was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital' (Treaty of Giyanti, 13 February 1755)

predecessors.note: Settled on the reviewer's decision: the Sunanate is born at the partition of 13 February 1755. Pakubuwono II's move from Kartasura to Sala (Solo) on 20 February 1745, which this page counts as the Sunanate's foundation, is the same dynasty on the same land: mataram-sultanate /ledger/34 records it as a capital move and /ledger/35 dissolves Mataram into this state and sultan-of-yogyakarta at Giyanti.

land.text: the Sunanate's lands after 'the territory of Surakarta Sunanate were reduced much further after the Java War'

successors.note: The sunanate continued as a protectorate state (infobox: 1806-1811 and 1816-1942), then as a Special Region until 16 June 1946; this dossier ends in 1830, as Cliopatria does (1829).

capitals.name: Surakarta (Sala, Solo)
capitals.note: The court moved to Sala (Solo) village on 20 February 1745 ('The date is considered the day that the Surakarta Sunanate was established', Surakarta page); the seat is Mataram's until Giyanti and the Sunanate's from 13 February 1755. The page does not date the palace's completion separately.

rulers.name: Pakubuwana III
rulers.note: Reign 15 December 1749 - 26 September 1788 (Surakarta table); 'recognizing Pakubuwono III (reigned 1749-55) as ruler of Surakarta' (Treaty of Giyanti page, citing Frederick and Worden 1993). Listed here from 1755, when the Sunanate begins; 1749-1755 is Mataram's last reign (Pakubuwana II died 20 December 1749).

rulers.name: Pakubuwana VI
rulers.note: Table ends 28 March 1830; deposed and exiled to Ambon in 1830 (Java War page).

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria outline (14 grid cells, 3,694 km2) but holding from 13 February 1755, not 1744: the state is created by the Treaty of Giyanti ('the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram ... was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital'); before that the land is Mataram's

keyframe_review.note: Years only. The Surakarta page gives no area to compare with 3,694 km2 (checked again). The outline is the core around Surakarta; from 1755 it no longer overlaps Mataram, which dissolves at Giyanti. The 'eastern half' of Mataram after 1755 is not drawn by the outline, and after the Java War the page says the territory 'were reduced much further', so the core is also the post-1830 remnant. The earlier verdict (holding from 20 February 1745) is withdrawn.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria outline, held to 1830, the year Pakubuwono VI was deposed and the Dutch annexed the remaining outlying lands

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria stops at 1829; the Java War ended in March 1830.

region.text: 'the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram in central Java was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital'; the page names no districts, the Cliopatria outline is the Surakarta core

ledger.note: 13 February 1755: the Treaty of Giyanti makes Surakarta a state under Pakubuwono III. 'On February 13, 1755, the Treaty of Giyanti was signed, dividing what was left of the kingdom of Mataram into two parts'; 'the eastern half of the Sultanate of Mataram ... was given to Pakubuwono III with Surakarta as its capital'. The Surakarta page counts 20 February 1745 as the day the Sunanate was established (Pakubuwono II's court moved to Sala), but under the one-state rule that is a capital move inside Mataram (mataram-sultanate /ledger/34). Region is the researcher's reading.

1755: the Sunanate is born a protectorate of the Dutch East India Company. Infobox: 'De jure protectorate state of the Dutch East India Company (1749-1799)' (the page starts it in 1749, before this dossier's start); also 'De facto independent state (1745-1800)'. Month 2 is the founding month, so that the ledger order holds. The Company has no polity row: the counterpart is the Dutch Republic, whose Cliopatria row holds its Indonesian possessions.

region.text: part of Surakarta, the Mangkunegaran princedom created 'after the Treaty of Salatiga (17 March 1757)'

ledger.note: 17 March 1757: the Treaty of Salatiga cuts the Mangkunegaran princedom out of Surakarta. The page calls it a further division of Surakarta and names no land, so the 6 km disc is a placeholder at the capital.
1799: the Company protectorate ends (infobox 1749-1799); the Batavian Republic follows.
1800: Batavian Republic protectorate. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the Batavian Republic within Dutch East Indies (1800-1806)'.
1806: protectorate of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the Kingdom of the Netherlands within Dutch East Indies (1806-1811; 1816-1942)'.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java (infobox 1806-1811).
1811: protectorate of the British East India Company. Infobox: 'Protectorate state of the British East India Company (1811-1816)'.
1816: the British protectorate ends (infobox 1811-1816); Java returns to the Dutch.

region.text: the mancanagara, the outlying lands the Dutch annexed after the Java War

ledger.note: 1830: the Sunanate is cut down. 'The territory of Surakarta Sunanate were reduced much further after the Java War (1825-1830)' and it had to cede much of its land to the Dutch; the Java War page names the mancanagara.

1830: this dossier ends with the Dutch cut of the mancanagara and the deposition of Pakubuwono VI; the infobox protectorate runs on to 1942 for the rump Sunanate, which is not drawn here. The end year is the dossier's, not the infobox's.

region.text: the Sunanate's remaining lands under Dutch control

ledger.note: 1830: Pakubuwono VI is deposed and exiled to Ambon, 'the Dutch suspected him of working with Diponegoro'; the rump princely states 'no longer posed a threat to the Dutch' (Java War page). The Sunanate continues as a protectorate state.

wars.name: Java War
wars.outcome: Pakubuwono VI, suspected of working with Diponegoro, was deposed and exiled to Ambon in 1830; the Sunanate lost most of its remaining outlying territory to the Dutch.
wars.note: Yogyakarta, not Surakarta, was the main theatre, so no zone is set for this dossier.

certainty.note: No boundary lines are named on the pages opened: the Giyanti halves, the Mangkunegaran cut and the mancanagara are all approximate.

notes:
Page budget 1-2 per state; the article was opened, Giyanti and the Java War shared with sultan-of-yogyakarta (cited in sources, ledger events cite the article and the Java War). (1) Founding: the page dates the Sunanate to 20 February 1745; the reviewer decided, and I followed, that the state starts at Giyanti on 13 February 1755 (see REVISION). (2) The outline is the Surakarta core only (14 cells); the 'eastern half' of Mataram after 1755 and the mancanagara are not drawn. (3) The sunanate did not end in 1830: protectorate state 1806-1811 and 1816-1942, Japanese protectorate 1942-1945, integration 19 August 1945, special region status aborted 16 June 1946 (page). The dossier ends at 1830 with Cliopatria. The protectorates of the infobox are now in this ledger (see REVISION); only Japan 1942-1945 lies outside the dossier. (4) Counterparts needing dossiers: mangkunegaran (created 17 March 1757; the page names no land), pakualaman (1813, from Yogyakarta). (5) Gazetteer name needed: Mancanegara; Kartasura. (6) The page's table gives Pakubuwana VI until 28 March 1830 (the day Diponegoro was arrested) while the Java War page has him deposed in 1830. The 1812 British period is on the Java War page, which does not mention Surakarta in it.

REVISION 2026-10-19 (after review): pages re-opened: Surakarta Sunanate, Treaty of Giyanti, Java War. (a) Start moved from 20 February 1745 to 13 February 1755 (identity.start, found event, capitals, certainty, rulers, predecessor land, keyframe text). The 1745 date stays in the found note and in the capital note. Agreed with the reviewer: under the one-state rule the 1745 move from Kartasura to Sala is a capital move inside Mataram (mataram-sultanate /ledger/34) and Mataram dissolves at Giyanti into this state and sultan-of-yogyakarta (/ledger/35). I note that the Surakarta page itself counts 1745 as the foundation and its infobox has 'De facto independent state (1745-1800)'. (b) The 1755 'split' event (counterpart sultan-of-yogyakarta) is deleted: the partition is Mataram's dissolve, and Yogyakarta's found names mataram-sultanate. (c) Rulers now start with Pakubuwana III from 1755 (reign 15 December 1749 - 26 September 1788 in the note); Pakubuwana II (1745-1749) is dropped because 1745-1749 is Mataram's. (d) Vassal pairs added, counterpart = the suzerain (rule 4 puts both sides in the vassal's ledger): dutch-republic 1755-1799 (infobox says 1749-1799; clipped to the dossier's start; the Company has no polity row), batavian-republic 1800-1806, dutch-east-indies 1806-1811, british-colonial-empire 1811-1816, dutch-east-indies 1816-1830 (the infobox runs to 1942; this dossier ends in 1830). The 1755 start carries month 2 only so that the ledger order holds; confidence 2. Not done (gap-fillers): the Mangkunegaran land of 1757 (6 km placeholder, confidence 1; the Java War page adds only that the Mangkunegaran Legion campaigned 'in Surakartan and Yogyakartan territory'), the eastern half of Mataram and the mancanagara (not drawn), the rump Sunanate 1830-1946. The page has no area figure (checked again). The page's table gives Pakubuwana VI to 28 March 1830, the Java War page has him deposed in 1830; the end year is 1830 either way.
